blogs.title: What Is a 1.58-bit LLM? The Ternary Twist Behind BitNet b1.58
blogs.description: Explain why BitNet b1.58 uses ternary weights {-1, 0, 1}, how that corresponds to 1.58 bits (three possible states), and what it means to train a Transformer with 1.58-bit weights and 8-bit activations without sacrificing accuracy.

blogs.title: From FP16 to Ternary: How BitNet b1.58 Matches Full-Precision LLMs
blogs.description: Walk through the head-to-head results versus FP16 LLaMA-like baselines: matching perplexity and zero-shot accuracy starting at 3B, being 2.71x faster and using 3.55x less GPU memory, and even outperforming the 3B FP16 model with a 3.9B 1.58-bit model.

blogs.title: Why Addition Beats Multiplication: The Compute Breakthrough of 1-bit LLMs
blogs.description: Demystify the compute model shift: replacing FP16 multiplies and adds with mostly INT8 additions in matrix multiplies, yielding massive arithmetic energy savings (71.4x for matmul on 7nm) and enabling faster throughput due to power constraints on chips.

blogs.title: Latency, Memory, Throughput: Real-World Speedups from 3B to 70B
blogs.description: Summarize practical wins measured with optimized kernels: up to 4.1x lower latency at 70B, large memory reductions, and 8.9x higher throughput on 70B using two 80GB A100s with pipeline parallelism (supporting 11x larger batch sizes).

blogs.title: A New Scaling Law: Rethinking Model Size vs. Inference Cost
blogs.description: Unpack the paper’s cost-performance equivalences showing that, for latency, memory, and energy, a 13B 1.58-bit model can be more efficient than a 3B FP16 model, 30B 1.58-bit than 7B FP16, and 70B 1.58-bit than 13B FP16.

blogs.title: Under the Hood: Quantization and LLaMA-Compatible Design Choices
blogs.description: Explain the absmean quantization that maps weights to {-1, 0, 1}, per-token activation scaling to [-Qb, Qb], and the LLaMA-alike stack (RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary, no biases) that lets BitNet b1.58 plug into Hugging Face, vLLM, and llama.cpp with minimal friction.

blogs.title: Training at Scale: 2 Trillion Tokens and Generalization with BitNet b1.58
blogs.description: Cover the 2T-token experiment using the StableLM-3B recipe, where BitNet b1.58 outperforms the StableLM 3B results across multiple benchmarks, highlighting that 1.58-bit models retain strong generalization when scaled in data.

blogs.title: Long Contexts and Edge Devices: New Frontiers for 1.58-bit LLMs
blogs.description: Detail how 8-bit activations halve KV-cache memory versus FP16 (with potential lossless compression to 4 bits), enabling longer contexts, and why the memory/energy profile makes CPU-friendly, on-device LLMs on edge and mobile far more viable.

blogs.title: MoE Meets 1-bit: Lower Memory, Lower Network, Higher Practicality
blogs.description: Discuss how 1.58-bit weights shrink MoE memory footprints and inter-chip communication, reducing device count and network overhead—and how this could enable larger expert counts or even single-chip deployments.

blogs.title: Hardware Futures: Designing Accelerators for 1-bit LLMs
blogs.description: Explore why the paper calls for hardware co-design—specialized datapaths for addition-heavy matmuls, smaller on-chip SRAM needs, and lower DRAM bandwidth—to fully realize the efficiency gains of 1.58-bit LLMs, building on trends seen in LLM-focused accelerators.

blogs.title: Greener AI by Design: Energy and Environmental Impacts of Ternary Weights
blogs.description: Translate the energy savings into environmental terms: fewer multiplications, less data movement, and lower power draw per token mean more sustainable LLM deployments at scale without compromising quality.

blogs.title: Adopting BitNet b1.58: A Practical Guide for ML Engineers
blogs.description: Offer a hands-on roadmap to trial and deploy 1.58-bit LLMs: training from scratch vs. post-training quantization, using LLaMA-like components, inference stacks (e.g., FasterTransformer, Ladder 2-bit kernels), and integration tips for production.
